pr.title: Allow the review loop's publish in the repository's Claude Code settings on init
pr.head: 218571ae49d10296d0ced3f6c92180c499d64c4b

summary: Claude Code's auto mode refuses project review publish for a clean review of a pull request the session's own account opened, as self-approval, so a review loop that runs as the author stalls on every clean head until a person runs the command. A repository cannot carry an autoMode exception, but it can carry an ordinary allow rule, which settles the command before the classifier runs.

So project init now adds Bash(project review publish *) to permissions.allow in the repository's committed .claude/settings.json. Because the rule exempts a command from the classifier, init adds it only when stdin is a terminal or --publish-rule is passed. Run without a terminal, as an agent refreshing the instructions runs it, init reports the file as kept with a note, and review.publish_rule can only turn the step off.

A settings file init cannot safely edit is kept with a note and init still exits 0. This repository commits the rule, review-changes says what the rule is for, and write_through moves out of ProjectStore so the new module can share it.

cards.title: What the rule authorizes
cards.html:
• One command, project review publish, with any arguments.
  • Every Claude Code session opened in a checkout that has the file, not only a review loop's.
  • That includes a changes-requested review and the real APPROVE that review.allow_approve permits on someone else's pull request.
  • publish's own checks still bound it: the head set up, the verdict matching the finding census, and the lock.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• d97b3e6: two findings. A bad review.publish_rule refused only after init had written files, and a plain-file .claude or a non-UTF-8 settings file aborted init with exit 65.
  • 2bec480 fixed both: the setting is read before any write, and both cases are kept with a note.
  • 218571a added the terminal gate and --publish-rule / --no-publish-rule. Reviewed clean.

cards.title: Host claims taken as given
cards.html: The change rests on two claims about Claude Code that the review did not check against the host: that a matching allow rule resolves before the auto-mode classifier, and that the workspace trust dialog lists a repository's allow rules before they apply.

groups.title: The rule and the settings file
groups.kicker: What gets written, where, and what is left alone
intro: allow_publish reads .claude/settings.json, appends the rule to permissions.allow when it is missing, and writes the file back as two-space JSON with every other setting kept. Each state it cannot safely edit returns a kept action whose note names the rule to add by hand.
With apply=False, the path an agent's init takes, a file that lacks the rule is reported rather than changed. This repository commits the file the new init writes.
concepts: The kept checks run in order: a link that leaves the repository, a .claude that is not a directory, a read or decode failure, invalid JSON, then an unexpected shape.
A file that already holds the rule reports unchanged whether or not apply is set.

checks.text: No path writes when apply is false: the only write_through call comes after the if not apply return.
A symlinked settings file inside the repository is written at its target, so the link stays a link.

files.note: The whole feature: the rule, the kept cases, and the apply switch.
This repository's copy, byte-for-byte what init writes.

groups.title: The terminal gate in init
intro: run decides the step before anything is written: an explicit flag wins, then review.publish_rule, and only then whether stdin is a terminal. The result is add, report, or nothing, and init appends the settings action after the instruction files.

The gate exists because the plan, implement and finish skills tell an agent to run project init to refresh a stale section. An agent's shell gives the command no terminal, so its init takes the note path.
concepts: Configuration can only turn the step off; review.publish_rule = true does not add the rule without a terminal.
The flags mirror --site and --no-site: passing either skips reading the setting.

checks.text: An invalid review.publish_rule refuses with exit 78 before store.init writes anything.
--publish-rule and --no-publish-rule share one dest, and the first action's None default is what an invocation without either sees.

files.note: The two flags in parser, publish_rule_enabled, and the gate in run.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Every scenario runs without a terminal unless it says otherwise
intro: The base test case now patches sys.stdin.isatty to false and seeds each repository with a settings file that already holds the rule, so the existing init tests report it unchanged. A test that stands for a person calls at_a_terminal.

New tests cover merging into existing settings, each kept case, the terminal gate with each flag and setting, and a bad setting refusing before any write. The site tests pass --no-publish-rule so they stay about the site.

checks.text: Only test_projector.py and test_site.py run init, so the suite does not depend on whether it runs at a terminal.

groups.title: Documentation and the review skill
groups.kicker: What people and agents are told
intro: The CLI guide adds .claude/settings.json to the files init manages, with the terminal gate, both flags, the kept cases, and the review.publish_rule key. The README says what a terminal run adds.
review-changes tells a reviewer to run publish as a command of its own so the rule matches, and, if the host still refuses it, to ask the user rather than retry or run init itself.
